title: Beyond Correctness: How Novice Software Engineering Students Exercise Oversight of Generative AI
abstract: arXiv:2610.32118v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is shifting software engineering students' work from producing artefacts towards evaluating and supervising AI-generated outputs. However, little is known about what characteristics students identify in outputs when reporting interventions, or how they exercise oversight during authentic software engineering work. We analysed 962 student-AI interaction turns documented by 145 first-year software engineering students through structured AI Journals, including 172 student-declared interventions. Using a multi-dimensional coding framework, we characterised the output characteristics identified in these reported interventions, students' reasons for intervening, the actions they took, and how those actions were enacted. translated_title: 超越正确性：软件工程新手学生如何对生成式AI行使监督
translated_abstract: 生成式人工智能（GenAI）正在将软件工程学生的工作重心从产出制品转向评估和监督AI生成的输出。然而，关于学生在报告干预时识别出输出具备哪些特征，或者他们在真实的软件工程工作中如何行使监督，目前知之甚少。我们分析了145名一年级软件工程学生通过结构化AI日志记录的962个学生-AI交互回合，其中包括172次学生声明的干预。通过多维编码框架，我们刻画了这些报告的干预中识别出的输出特征、学生干预的原因、他们采取的行动以及这些行动的实施方式。74.4%的干预中发现了适用性问题，而涉及正确性问题的仅占16.9%，这表明监督更多关注的是看似合理的AI输出是否真正适合于
tldr: 软件工程新手学生对生成式AI的监督主要聚焦于输出的适用性问题（74.4%）而非正确性问题（16.9%），表明学生监督的核心是判断看似合理的AI输出是否真正适合实际任务。
en_tdlr: Novice software engineering students exercise oversight of GenAI primarily around fitness problems (74.4%) rather than correctness problems (16.9%), indicating that their supervision centers on judging whether plausible AI outputs are actually suitable for the task.
